races.name: Racing TV Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Rialannah
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with strong recent form who should relish this tactical setup under in-form Gavin Sheehan

runners_data.name: Tropical Speed
runners_data.note: Late-running type returning from 137-day break but showed winning form last time and handles good ground well

runners_data.name: Breezethroughlife
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who can track the pace and has winning form on good ground, though 31 days off

runners_data.name: Ilitch
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose best form came on good ground but recent efforts have been disappointing

runners_data.name: Mahon Falls
runners_data.note: Prominent type with consistent recent form but yet to win over hurdles and carries inexperienced jockey

runners_data.name: Alan Bresil
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with 12lb weight advantage but poor recent form suggests he's out of sorts

runners_data.name: The Wise Traveller
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with significant weight advantage who ran just 7 days ago and could surprise

runners_data.name: Raby Mere
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in good form with strong record on good ground, though inexperienced jockey claims 3lb

races.paceDynamic: The Wise Traveller will take them along at a steady gallop from the front with no serious pace pressure in this small field. Breezethroughlife, Mahon Falls and Raby Mere can track prominently but are unlikely to challenge The Wise Traveller's early control. With most runners preferring to settle and come late (Rialannah, Tropical Speed, Ilitch, Alan Bresil), the pace will build gradually through the middle sections before quickening from the final hurdle. This tactical setup strongly favours hold-up horses who can deliver late runs, as the early pace will be manageable and the finish will become a sprint.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If The Wise Traveller sets a steady early gallop and the field bunches approaching two out
scenarios.body: The moderate pace allows closers to deliver perfectly timed challenges, with the race becoming a stamina test in the final furlong. Rialannah, Tropical Speed and Ilitch can all unleash finishing kicks from off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent tracker strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Breezethroughlife or Raby Mere track The Wise Traveller closely and kick approaching the last
scenarios.body: The prominent runners can steal a march on the hold-up brigade by making their move before the field organizes. Their tactical positioning gives them first run on horses still finding their stride.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Wire-to-wire shock
scenarios.trigger: If The Wise Traveller maintains strong fractions and the field fails to close
scenarios.body: The 10-year-old's recent proximity to better horses suggests untapped reserves, and his 12lb weight advantage could prove decisive. Hold-up horses get their timing wrong or meet traffic problems.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical mess benefits outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the field goes very slowly early and turns into a sprint from the home turn
scenarios.body: The change of pace catches favorites napping while an unfancied runner finds the gaps. The moderate early pace negates stamina advantages and makes it purely about speed.

watchPoints.text: The Wise Traveller could steal this if he maintains strong fractions and the 12lb weight advantage tells
Tropical Speed's 137-day absence is a major concern despite his winning last-time-out form
Breezethroughlife needs to overcome 31 days off but his prominent style suits this tactical setup perfectly
Both Quinlan brothers ride prominent runners (Shane on Mahon Falls, Jack on Breezethroughlife) and could dictate tactics
Rialannah's hold-up style is perfectly suited to this race shape if Gavin Sheehan times his challenge correctly

races.name: Weatherbys nhstallions.co.uk Mares' Handicap Chase (Queen Boudicca Mares' Chase Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Moviddy
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who needs a strong pace to be effective, carrying top weight but has solid recent form and experience at this level.

runners_data.name: Gilbertina
runners_data.note: Prominent runner likely to go forward early, Tom Midgley's 3lb claim useful but trainer's poor recent record (0/7) is concerning.

runners_data.name: Fortunefavorsdbold
runners_data.note: Another front-runner who could press Gilbertina for the lead, Christian Williams stable in better form and horse has shown consistency in similar company.

runners_data.name: Annie Nail
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with significant weight advantage, won last time out and represents a trainer with excellent recent strike-rate (1/2).

runners_data.name: Ballygelly
runners_data.note: Backmarker who needs everything to fall right, carries bottom weight but has been inconsistent with multiple pulls-ups recently.

races.paceDynamic: Gilbertina will likely lead or share early duties with Fortunefavorsdbold, both prominent runners with decent recent form. With only five runners and no confirmed tearaway pace-setter, this shapes as a measured gallop over the extended three-mile trip. The three hold-up horses (Moviddy, Annie Nail, Ballygelly) will need the pace to quicken sufficiently in the final mile to unleash their finishing kicks. This tactical setup clearly favours the front-running and prominent types who can control the tempo and avoid getting caught in a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Gilbertina or Fortunefavorsdbold establishes an uncontested lead and dictates a steady tempo
scenarios.body: The leader can measure out their effort over the long trip and prove difficult to peg back when the closers make their move. Hold-up horses struggle to make up meaningful ground in what becomes a test of stamina rather than speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent duo go too fast early or engage in a pace battle through the middle stages
scenarios.body: The increased tempo sets up perfectly for the three hold-up horses to produce their trademark finishing kicks. Annie Nail and Moviddy particularly thrive when able to pick off tiring leaders.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Weight Advantage Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the race becomes a true stamina test where the 22-23lb weight advantage of the bottom weights tells
scenarios.body: Annie Nail and Ballygelly can use their significant weight concessions to outlast the higher-rated but burden-carrying rivals. The extended trip amplifies the importance of every pound carried.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Class Rises to Top
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops into a genuine Group-level contest where superior ratings and experience matter most
scenarios.body: The three horses rated 96-97 (Moviddy, Gilbertina, Fortunefavorsdbold) assert their class advantage despite tactical disadvantages. Recent form and proven ability at this level becomes the deciding factor.

watchPoints.text: Gilbertina and Fortunefavorsdbold engaging in an early speed duel that could set up the race for the closers
Annie Nail getting too far back early given her hold-up style and the likelihood of a modest pace
Ballygelly's jumping under pressure, given her recent history of unseating and pulling up
The overall pace through the first two miles, as a truly dawdled gallop would compromise the hold-up horses' chances
Tom Midgley's handling of Gilbertina in the early stages, as his inexperience could lead to tactical errors

races.name: Woodfordes Mares' Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Honey I'm Good
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent runner who should track Natus Vincere, but 68 days off and advancing years are concerns for Miss Eleanor Williams.

runners_data.name: Dartmouth Rose
runners_data.note: Recent winner who relies on hold-up tactics, needs the pace to develop properly but Jack Quinlan knows how to time a challenge.

runners_data.name: Silver Gale
runners_data.note: High TopSpeed rating but dangerous finishing problems highlighted, needs everything to fall right for Gavin Sheehan and Katy Price.

runners_data.name: Natus Vincere
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with class edge gets Sean Bowen in the saddle, only 29 days since last run suits Olly Murphy's approach.

races.paceDynamic: Natus Vincere will control this small field from the front, setting a manageable gallop over this extended trip without meaningful early pressure. Honey I'm Good may track in second, but her prominent style won't challenge the leader early. The hold-up pair of Dartmouth Rose and Silver Gale will rely on the pace quickening late, but with only one genuine leader, the tempo may prove too steady for closers to peg back. This race shape strongly favors front-running and prominent runners who can dictate terms without pace pressure.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Natus Vincere Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Natus Vincere jumps well and sets his own tempo from the front
scenarios.body: The leader faces minimal early pressure and can quicken when it matters, making life difficult for the hold-up horses. Sean Bowen's mount has the class edge and tactical advantage in this small field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Dartmouth Charge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves too steady and Dartmouth Rose gets a strong ride from Quinlan
scenarios.body: The hold-up mare benefits from her recent winning form and gets first run on the field when the pace lifts. Her superior finishing speed tells over this longer trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Honey I'm Good Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Natus Vincere makes jumping errors or doesn't see out the extended trip
scenarios.body: Honey I'm Good can track the leader and strike when he weakens, using her prominent running style to maximum effect. The 10-year-old's consistency gives her claims if the favorite falters.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Silver Gale Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Silver Gale overcomes her finishing problems and gets an inspired Sheehan ride
scenarios.body: The youngest horse in the field could benefit from a truly-run race and her high TopSpeed rating. However, her tendency to fade makes this an unlikely outcome despite Gavin Sheehan's presence.

watchPoints.text: Silver Gale's finishing problems could resurface under pressure despite Gavin Sheehan's skill in the saddle
Honey I'm Good's 68-day absence may leave her short of peak fitness for Miss Eleanor Williams in this company
Natus Vincere's jumping quality early will determine how comfortably he can control the tempo for Sean Bowen
Dartmouth Rose needs the pace to develop late enough for Jack Quinlan to deliver her finishing kick
The small field size reduces the likelihood of a strong early gallop that would favor the hold-up horses

races.name: Woodfordes Supports Dereham Meeting Point Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Slaney Opera
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with strong recent form including a narrow second last time, benefits from the likely tactical pace scenario

runners_data.name: Esperti
runners_data.note: Versatile hold-up type with solid recent efforts, particularly effective when able to use turn of foot from off the pace

runners_data.name: Prince Cleni
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who will likely dictate terms but faces tactical disadvantage if pace becomes too slow early

runners_data.name: Blackacre
runners_data.note: Fresh after 175-day break which could be asset or liability, needs the pace to be strong to utilize stamina over sprint finish

races.paceDynamic: Prince Cleni will likely dictate from the front in this small field, with all four runners naturally preferring to settle behind the pace. With no genuine pace pressers, Prince Cleni can bowl along at a comfortable gallop without harassment through the early stages. The lack of early speed means the race will develop into a tactical affair where positioning and stamina management become crucial over this extended trip. This setup clearly favours horses with tactical speed and the ability to quicken from off the pace, giving hold-up performers the edge over pure front-runners.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tactical Hold-Up Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Prince Cleni sets uncontested fractions and the pace stays moderate
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where horses with the best turn of foot prevail from tracking positions. Slaney Opera and Esperti benefit most from their tactical speed and recent form edge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Extended Gallop Grind
scenarios.trigger: If the genuine pace creates a true staying test throughout
scenarios.body: Prince Cleni's front-running advantage grows as stamina becomes the deciding factor over pure speed. Blackacre's fresh legs after a long break could prove valuable in a gruelling finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Early Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Prince Cleni goes too slow early and gets swamped
scenarios.body: The race turns into a messy sprint where any horse can win from the resulting bunched finish. Form and class become secondary to position and luck in running.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prince Cleni Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Prince Cleni gets perfect uncontested splits and stays on strongly
scenarios.body: The front-runner capitalizes on soft fractions to maintain his advantage all the way to the line. His recent efforts suggest he has the stamina to make it pay at this trip.

watchPoints.text: Prince Cleni's early pace-setting - if he goes too slowly he becomes vulnerable to being swamped by tactical types
Blackacre's fitness after 175 days off - fresh legs could be decisive or lack of race sharpness could show
Slaney Opera's jumping under pressure - needs to maintain fluency when the race develops in the closing stages
The pace through the middle stages - moderate fractions will favour the hold-up horses significantly

races.name: Weatherbys Design & Print Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Jamada
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with highest ratings but 52 days since last outing may leave him short of peak fitness despite Sean Bowen's strong partnership with Olly Murphy

runners_data.name: Crackalackin
runners_data.note: Front-runner making hurdles debut for in-form Newland/Insole team, likely to dictate terms but Luke Scott's inexperience could prove costly at crucial moments

runners_data.name: Sense Of Reason
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist switching from Fellowes' Flat operation with poor recent form suggesting he needs everything to fall perfectly to compete with this field

runners_data.name: Somkiyr
runners_data.note: Prominent runner from struggling Irvine yard with low ratings but Freddie Mitchell's claim valuable and recent proximity to better horses suggests competitiveness

races.paceDynamic: Crackalackin will lead from the front with Somkiyr likely tracking in second, creating a modest early gallop in this small field. The lack of genuine pace pressure means Crackalackin can dictate terms without being harried, setting up a controlled tempo that builds gradually. Hold-up horses Jamada and Sense Of Reason will have plenty of time to get organized from off the pace. This sustainable pace scenario strongly favours the front-running and prominent racers who can avoid traffic complications and kick clear when the tempo lifts approaching the final flight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Crackalackin Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Crackalackin jumps cleanly and maintains a steady rhythm without serious pressure
scenarios.body: Luke Scott can dictate ideal fractions and time his effort perfectly, while the hold-up horses struggle to peg back his advantage. The leader's class edge combined with tactical control proves decisive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Jamada's Class Shows Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes too sedate and Jamada gets a clear run from the back
scenarios.body: Sean Bowen can utilize Jamada's superior ratings and proven form to sweep past tired leaders in the final furlong. The hold-up specialist's higher class tells when it matters.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Somkiyr Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Somkiyr can stay close to Crackalackin and both front-runners maintain their advantage
scenarios.body: The prominent runner can capitalize on any jumping errors from the leader while keeping the hold-up horses at bay. His recent runs suggest he's capable of better than his low rating indicates.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Sense Of Reason Revival
scenarios.trigger: If Tom Cannon can secure the perfect trip and the pace collapses completely
scenarios.body: The Charlie Fellowes-trained runner can exploit his flat racing speed in a sprint finish scenario. However, his recent form suggests this outcome relies heavily on everything falling perfectly into place.

watchPoints.text: Crackalackin's jumping technique on hurdles debut - any significant errors will immediately compromise his front-running tactics and hand initiative to rivals
Jamada's early positioning given Sean Bowen needs to overcome 52-day absence while securing clear passage from hold-up position in small field
Luke Scott and Freddie Mitchell both carrying inexperience - watch for tactical errors or misjudged timing from either rider in closing stages
Early pace development crucial - if Crackalackin goes too fast or too slow it completely changes the tactical dynamic for hold-up horses

races.name: Sandcliff Cromer "Grassroots" Maiden Hunters' Chase (For The Turner Trophy)

runners_data.name: On Lovers Walk
runners_data.note: Front-running style gives huge tactical advantage with only hold-up horses behind, 242 days off but proven over course and distance

runners_data.name: Mister Splash
runners_data.note: Hold-up style disadvantaged by lack of early pace, trainer has no recent runners but horse showed decent form before long break

runners_data.name: Chapelier
runners_data.note: 14-year-old veteran faces traffic problems with hold-up style, long absence of 1427 days is major concern despite recent form

runners_data.name: Royal Cave
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with shortest break at 263 days, needs to overcome tactical disadvantage of similar styles ahead of him

races.paceDynamic: On Lovers Walk will likely lead from the start with no obvious pace pressure in this small field of four. Mister Splash, Chapelier, and Royal Cave are all hold-up horses who will settle behind the leader. This creates a tactical nightmare for the three hold-up runners who must time their challenges perfectly from similar positions. The lack of early pace pressure strongly favours the front-running profile of On Lovers Walk.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If On Lovers Walk gets an uncontested lead and maintains a sustainable gallop
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows the leader to dictate fractions and kick clear when the hold-up horses are still organising their challenges. With three similar tactical horses behind, none can gain a decisive positional advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Success
scenarios.trigger: If one of the hold-up horses gets the perfect split and times their run to perfection
scenarios.body: The patient tactics pay off as the hold-up runner benefits from the steady early pace to deliver a perfectly-timed challenge. The front runner's long stint in front takes its toll in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the three hold-up horses interfere with each other's runs in the closing stages
scenarios.body: Poor positioning and lack of room causes the three similar-styled runners to hamper each other's finishing kicks. On Lovers Walk capitalises on the tactical mess behind to pull clear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Veteran Experience Tells
scenarios.trigger: If Chapelier's 14-year-old experience helps him find the best route home
scenarios.body: The oldest horse uses guile and racecraft to navigate around traffic problems that stymie his younger rivals. Age and cunning overcome youth and inexperience in a tactical finish.

watchPoints.text: On Lovers Walk jumping - any early mistake would hand initiative to the three hold-up horses behind
Traffic problems in straight - three hold-up horses could interfere with each other's finishing runs
Mister Splash early positioning - needs to be closer than usual given lack of pace pressure
Chapelier handling the trip - 14-year-old returning after long break over this demanding distance
Royal Cave getting clear run - must avoid being trapped behind horses when making move
